newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW-Japan October current account data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Japan October current account data.

text.p: Following are a selection of initial reactions from economists and analysts to Japan's October current account data. The government said on Wednesday that Japan's October current account surplus fell 19.6 percent from a year earlier to 367.4 billion yen.
MAMORU YAMAZAKI, PARIBAS CAPITAL MARKETS, TOKYO:
"The data were in line with our forecasts. The year-on-year decline in the current account surplus is gradually narrowing. We confirmed that trend."

Yamazaki told Reuters Financial Television he expects the year-on-year surplus to continue to shrink for a while, but added that Japan may at some point next year see year-on-year growth in both its current account and trade balance surpluses.
With machinery orders and private capital spending picking up, current economic activity was stronger than was generally expected, Yamazaki said.
"But at the same time, everybody is concerned about the weak economic activity due to the planned consumption tax hike next April," Yamazaki said.
